pointOfView: A calm, tool-like pricing section where the price is the loudest thing on each plan and the recommended plan is obvious without shouting.
brief: Three per-seat plans for a developer platform. Web, light and dark themes, must work at 390px. Worked example for the Seenry skill.

decisions.choice: One container divided by hairlines, not three floating cards
decisions.why: Plans read as one comparison. Separate shadowed cards compete with each other and misalign when copy lengths differ.
decisions.evidence: Vercel and Linear pricing pages, inspected through Seenry MCP

decisions.choice: CSS subgrid for plan, price, description, button and features
decisions.why: Buttons and feature lists line up across plans whatever the description length, which the leaders do by hand and we get for free.

decisions.choice: Only the recommended plan's button is filled; a small badge names it
decisions.why: One primary action per view. Scaling or tinting the whole card is the common AI tell.
The price is the answer people came for. Light-to-medium weight and tight tracking match the measured leaders (Vercel 40/500, Stripe display weight 300).

decisions.choice: “Everything in Hobby, plus:” before each feature list
decisions.why: Shows only what changes between plans, so lists stay short and comparable.

research.method: Seenry MCP (list_sites, get_page, get_screenshot section=Pricing, get_design)

references.name: Vercel pricing
references.seen: Three plans in one bordered container split by 1px lines; plan name small, price large; “All Hobby features, plus:”; only the Pro button filled.
references.measured: Hero 64/400 −0.06em; pill buttons; radius 6–8 on controls
references.adopt: Shared container, inheritance line, one filled button
references.avoid: An icon before every feature line

references.name: Linear pricing
references.seen: Hairline columns, plan name and price at the top, buttons aligned at the bottom of every column.
references.adopt: Buttons on one line across plans

references.name: Notion pricing
references.seen: Two plans, large prices, full-width tinted buttons, “Everything in Free, and:”.
references.avoid: Full-width tinted buttons on every plan

references.name: Stripe pricing
references.seen: The price itself is the display type (3.4% + 30¢); custom plan on a dark panel beside the standard one.

tableStakes: Three plans, the middle one recommended
A contact-sales plan at the top end
edge: Plans in one container with hairlines
opening: Per-seat math next to the price
Subgrid alignment that survives any copy length

variants.name: A. Shared container
variants.why: Rows align across plans; the price leads; one filled button. Audits clean at both widths.

variants.name: B. Floating cards
variants.why: Three shadows compete, the recommended card has to be scaled to stand out, and buttons drift when a description wraps.

variants.name: C. Comparison table first
variants.why: Precise but slow to scan on a phone; kept as a separate section below the plans.

color.why: Neutral surfaces do the work so the one indigo button is the only colored action on the page. Indigo reads as a calm, technical accent and keeps white text above WCAG AA.

type.why: A neutral tool voice for a developer product. Tuned with cv11 and ss01, tightened for display sizes.

scale.sample: For professionals shipping to production every week.

spec.Grid: 4px base · 24 inset on all sides · container r16 with a ring
spec.Rows: subgrid: plan, price, description, button, features
spec.Gaps: plan → price 16 · price → description 8 · description → button 24 · button → features 24
spec.Keylines: every element starts on the 24 inset; check icons pulled left so their ink sits on it
spec.Color: one filled accent button; other plans use the outlined secondary button

guidelines.rule: Plans share one container divided by hairlines. Never float plans as separate shadowed cards.
guidelines.do: One container, 1px dividers, rows aligned with subgrid
guidelines.dont: Three cards with drop shadows and a scaled-up middle card

guidelines.rule: Only the recommended plan gets the filled accent button. Everything else stays neutral.
guidelines.dont: A filled button on every plan, or a tinted card background

guidelines.rule: The price is the largest thing in a plan: 40px, weight 500, tabular figures.
guidelines.do: $16 / seat / month with the period in secondary text
guidelines.dont: Bold 700 prices, or a plan name larger than its price

guidelines.rule: Each paid plan lists only what it adds, introduced by “Everything in X, plus:”.
guidelines.dont: Repeating every feature from the plan below

guidelines.rule: Check icons align by their ink to the text edge, one icon set, 16px, accent-text color.
guidelines.dont: Mixed icon sets, or icons boxed and indented

checks.name: System, alignment and optical audit at 1440 and 390
Contrast in light and dark (WCAG AA and APCA)
Billing toggle updates prices, keyboard reachable
